text:
Maya P: Did a focused perf sweep on canary overnight. Noticed consistent decode-dominated tails on several low-token routes. Prefill is fine aside from occasional KV misses, but decode p99 is killing our SLOs. Sharing a short summary + traces. @Ajay @Sam @Elaine @Ryan

Ajay: Quick numbers from the sweep (20k calls, mixed seq lengths):
- prefill: p50 20ms, p95 55ms, p99 110ms
- decode: p50 45ms, p95 210ms, p99 520ms
- KV miss extra: +60-150ms (correlates with cold prefixes)
Trace link: https://perf.redwood/trace/ef56c9 (one example with long decode queue)

Sam: Sounds like decode queuing + batching is the common factor. In a bunch of traces the decode_queue grows to >200ms before exec even starts. For short-response routes that’s unacceptable. I propose per-route latency sensitivity tags and separate microbatch caps: decode_cap small for latency-sensitive routes.

Elaine: Kernel note: our current kernel selector optimizes for throughput by preferring a dense attention kernel; it performs poorly for short decode lengths because of setup overhead. We should consider a lightweight short-seq kernel for decode when expected output tokens < 32, even if aggregate throughput drops slightly. Also exploring a decode-only int8 path (needs eval).

Ryan: KV patterns: hot prefixes are sometimes pinned to a single shard leading to spikes on that shard. Two mitigations: async post-prefill prefetch for top-N keys predicted by prefix model, and a shard hotness rebalancer that moves hot prefixes across shards gradually. Prefetch config draft below.

perf-bot: Canary perf run: https://ci.redwood/build/1756014000/perf -- includes per-stage hist CSV and raw counters

infra-bot: Canary deployed with trace flags branch decode-shortseq-fixes at 1756014330

Ajay: Proposed experiment matrix (short):
1) Kernel switch: short-seq kernel for decode when expected_decode_tokens < 32. Measure per-route p95/p99.
2) Decode microbatch cap: hard cap=3 for latency-sensitive routes; soft cap adaptive for others (based on queue length and remaining tail budget).
3) KV async prefetch: trigger on prefill completion for top-2 predicted keys.
4) Instrument stage-level spans: prefill_queue, prefill_exec, kv_fetch, decode_queue, decode_exec.
I'll implement 1+4. @Ryan take 3.

Sam: I'll implement route-level SLO tags and the A/B canary framework (50/50 split) for these toggles. Need the perf rig to emit stage histograms.

Elaine: On quantization: int8 decode could reduce decode_exec by ~15-30% in microbenchmarks. We need to run our regression suite (LLM-regen + safety + hallucination tests) and set a quality threshold. I'll prep harness and scoreboard.

Ryan: Prefetch config prototype: 

```
kv.prefetch.enabled=true
kv.prefetch.top_k=2
kv.prefetch.min_confidence=0.65
kv.prefetch.mode=async
kv.prefetch.backoff_ms=50
```
Also drafting a shard hotness rebalancer that migrates keys when a shard's 1m p99 exceeds threshold. Will run 24h hot-spot canary.

Maya P: Example of desired per-request stage timeline (we should emit this shape from runtime):
```
{
  request_id: "req_789",
  timeline: [
    {stage: "prefill_queue", start_ms: 0, end_ms: 10},
    {stage: "prefill_exec", start_ms: 10, end_ms: 48},
    {stage: "kv_fetch", start_ms: 48, end_ms: 120},
    {stage: "decode_queue", start_ms: 120, end_ms: 180},
    {stage: "decode_exec", start_ms: 180, end_ms: 420}
  ]
}
```
If we consistently surface these spans we can split tail contributions across queueing, kv, and exec.

Sam: For adaptive caps I suggest a simple token-estimator at enqueue: estimate_out_tokens = model.sample_output_estimate(request); if estimate_out_tokens < 8 then decode_cap=1 else decode_cap = min(global_decode_cap, floor(budget/est_out)). Also track per-route rolling p99 to override caps.

Elaine: Regression gating for int8: require no more than 0.5% drop on our quality scoreboard across a 2000-prompt sample, and no safety-critical failures. Also require per-route rollback hooks.

Ajay: Bench plan: run kernel A (current) vs kernel B (short-seq) on 50k short-seq requests across 4 GPU types, collect per-stage histograms and CPU/GPU counters. Metric: change in decode p99 (absolute ms) and p99 tokens/sec.

Ryan: I'll stress-test prefetch under heavy hot-prefix churn to watch for increased KV load or cascading misses. Will add circuit-breaker that disables prefetch if KV error rate or latency crosses threshold.

Maya P: Prioritization (short):
- Immediate: kernel heuristic + stage tracing (fast win for attribution).
- High: decode microbatch caps per-route + A/B canary.
- Medium: KV prefetch + shard rebalancer.
- Low: int8 decode path (pending regression pass).

Action items recap:
- Ajay: implement short-seq kernel selector + stage span emissions.
- Sam: route SLO tags + canary A/B + perf aggregator changes.
- Ryan: KV prefetch prototype + shard rebalancer + circuit breaker.
- Elaine: int8 regression harness + quality scoreboard.
- Maya P: run sweep baseline and coordinate reviews.

Maya P: Schedule a sync tomorrow 09:30 to review canary baselines and initial numbers. Thanks all :thumbsup:
